A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GMValuator and contain the same main sections and Appendices A-P. All 27 pages support comparison; 25 render identically, with differences confined to pages 1 and 4.

before.justification: v8 reports original class/attribute matching, noisy-data detection and efficiency experiments in Section 4, plus statistical tests, sensitivity studies and additional evaluations in the appendices.

after.justification: v9 retains the original experiments and their numerical and visual outcomes in Section 4 and the appendices, including the Stable Diffusion evaluation in Appendix N.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1-3.3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same quantization-based recall, similarity re-ranking, image-quality calibration and contribution aggregation procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same MNIST, CIFAR-10, ImageNet, CelebA, AFHQ, FFHQ and Naruto coverage, including the same noisy-data and text-to-image scenarios.

E2.justification: VAE-TracIn remains in Tables 2 and 4, and IF4GAN remains in Figure 5 and Table 4. Comparisons among GMValuator variants and against nearest-neighbor search in Appendix P are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4 and the appendices retain the same evaluation criteria, model configurations, top-k settings, sample sizes, noise construction and timing procedures.

E4.justification: The generated-sample-size sensitivity study, embedding and distance comparisons, calibration ablations, scalability study and quantization-recall analysis in Appendices F-I and O-P are unchanged.

E5.justification: Appendix D retains the same t-tests, p-values and 0.01 significance threshold. Appendix F still reports means and standard deviations over 10 runs, with no change in uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: All numerical entries, result figures and reported findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 2 retains the 77.27% ImageNet identical-class score for GMValuator using DreamSim at k=30.

T1.justification: The definitions, assumptions, Theorem 2.4 and Appendix M proof are identical. Removing '(Jiaxi: S* in the appendix)' before Equation (3) deletes an editorial note without changing the mathematical statement or reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about model-agnostic, training-free data valuation through similarity matching, quality calibration and four evaluation criteria.

C2.justification: Interpretations of performance and efficiency, explanations of re-ranking and calibration, possible applications in Appendix K, and the vision-only limitation and proposed NLP extension in Appendix L remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v9 removes the abstract's code-availability statement and the paper's only explicit GMValuator repository link, without replacing it elsewhere. Algorithm and implementation details remain unchanged. This establishes a loss of access information, not that the repository itself became unavailable.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, Appendix C and reference list are unchanged. No cited work or substantive positioning relative to prior research is added or removed.

P1.justification: v9 deletes the abstract's code-access sentence and the stray author note beside Theorem 2.4, and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. The remaining prose and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: The shortened abstract slightly reflows the first page. Figures, tables, captions and their placement remain unchanged, as do all appendix layouts.

improvement.justification: Removing the stray author note improves polish, but deleting the sole explicit implementation link reduces the paper's usefulness for locating and reproducing the code. With the scientific content and supporting evidence unchanged, the loss of code-access guidance outweighs the small editorial benefit.
